canonical_policy.name: Git mutations require explicit request
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete branches, or perform other repository-changing Git operations unless explicitly requested.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Root explicit-request gate conflicts potentially with approved-workflow permission and package-manifest commit instruction. Both tensions are already registered, as is stronger non-rewritable protected/shared-branch language. No approval inferred from a workflow description.

Whether a repository-changing operation may happen at all is governed by `CLAUDE.md` § Git (explicit request only; parallel work on separate branches/worktrees).
- Before any repository-changing operation, inspect the relevant state (`git status`, `git diff`, `git diff --cached`, current branch, upstream) and use the minimum operation that achieves the request; never silently clean unrelated working-tree changes.
- High-risk operations — `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, `git push --force`, `git push --force-with-lease`, branch deletion, rebasing shared history — run only when explicitly requested or required by an approved workflow, and only after inspecting what will be lost or rewritten. Treat `main`, `master`, and other protected or shared branches as non-rewritable.

- Follow an existing branch-naming convention; otherwise prefixes such as `feature/`, `fix/`, `refactor/`, `test/`, `docs/`, `chore/` are reasonable. Do not rename an existing user branch to fit.
- One branch is never checked out in several normal worktrees at once; keep each worktree focused on its branch.

- Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete branches, or perform other repository-changing Git operations unless explicitly requested.
- Parallel implementation work must use separate branches or worktrees; keep unrelated changes out of the current branch.

canonical_policy.name: Decision control protocol
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Classify decisions as Decided, Delegated, or Reserved; Reserved changes require explicit approval and headless runs must not silently alter architecture.

4. Run the checker and fix every reported item:

`SPECIFICATION.md`, `CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md`, feature specifications, and task prompts are inputs, not instruction layers. They may request a decision change; they never silently override engineering policy.

- **Decided** — settled by the imported decision files, approved product sources, or recorded decisions: follow it; reopening requires approval.
- **Delegated** — local, reversible, and does not materially change a boundary, dependency, accepted convention, public contract, or observable behavior: decide and proceed.
- **Reserved** — requires approval: changing an accepted project/architecture decision; adopting a new architectural style or pattern (Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns, CQRS, mediator-based organization, Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, a project-wide Result model, microservices); adding a production project/layer or changing the project reference graph; changing persistence boundaries (for example several persistence contexts) or persistence technology; adding an infrastructure category (messaging, background processing, distributed cache, search, external storage, external identity); adding a major library/framework or replacing approved baseline technology; introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction; changing authentication/authorization architecture; a breaking public API change or adopting API versioning; defining product behavior or tunable values not defined by product sources; changing a capability selection (also requires an ADR).
- Unclear case: any "yes" makes it Reserved — does it add, remove, or replace a dependency, framework, or infrastructure capability? change a project/layer/reference boundary? establish a convention other code must follow? change observable behavior or a public contract? become expensive to reverse once other code depends on it?
- For a Reserved decision, send a Decision Request (Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked, Proceeding with) and continue only with non-Reserved work. Do not ask for approval for routine choices already constrained by the specification, approved stack, existing code, or rules.
- An explicit user instruction counts as approval; record the accepted decision with `architecture-decision`. In autonomous/headless runs, take only a policy-compliant non-Reserved path and report unresolved Decision Requests explicitly.

canonical_policy.name: Never discard user changes
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean, or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Stash-away ban and preservation before worktree removal are independently stronger than destructive reset prohibition, but explicit in replica and challenged by independent. Keep prior uncertainty about authorized recoverable stashing.

- High-risk operations — `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, `git push --force`, `git push --force-with-lease`, branch deletion, rebasing shared history — run only when explicitly requested or required by an approved workflow, and only after inspecting what will be lost or rewritten. Treat `main`, `master`, and other protected or shared branches as non-rewritable.
- One branch is never checked out in several normal worktrees at once; keep each worktree focused on its branch.
- Before removing a worktree, confirm its changes are committed or otherwise preserved; never remove a worktree holding uncommitted user work.
- Before pushing: confirm the intended branch, understand the working/staged state, ensure relevant verification completed, and avoid pushing unrelated local commits.
- Choose merge or rebase by repository convention or the user's request, not preference. Inspect uncommitted work first; never stash, reset, or discard automatically to let the operation proceed.
- Resolve conflicts by the intended combined behavior, not by mechanically taking "ours" or "theirs"; run relevant verification afterwards.
